title: Sheinbaum Says Government Will Assist Migrant Caravans Without Repression
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [November 12, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/gobierno-atendera-
caravanas-migrantes-sin-represion-afirma-sheinbaum/), an investigative Mexican
news outlet._

Assistance to migrant caravans making their way through Mexico will continue
without repressive measures and with respect for human rights, President
**Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** assured, responding to the warning from her US
counterpart, **Donald Trump** , that he would double tariffs if the country
does not halt their advance toward the United States.

During her morning press conference, the president maintained that the
**National Migration Institute (INM)** has experience assisting these groups,
informing them about restrictions on entering US territory and facilitating
the return of those who decide to go back to their countries of origin.

Sheinbaum explained that around 10 caravans, or possibly more, have arrived
over the past two years. In these cases, the authorities individually inform
their members about immigration conditions in the United States and offer them
basic care during their stay in Mexico.

According to the president, most people decide to return to their country
after receiving this information. The government facilitates that return and
seeks to ensure that, while they remain in national territory, they receive
care and their human rights are respected.

The INM takes part in the work of accompanying migrants, along with, depending
on the needs of each case, the Undersecretariat for Human Rights, the
Secretariat of Well-being and the **National Guard**. Sheinbaum clarified that
the involvement of the latter force does not seek to repress or use violence,
but to accompany migrants and provide them with information.

Asked about the possibility of reinforcing the military presence on the
southern border as new caravans advance, the president stated that no special
response is required, given the experience accumulated by federal
institutions.

The head of the federal executive branch warned that some people deceive
migrants by telling them that the **outcome of the elections in the United
States** changed that country’s immigration policy. She described that
information as false and maintained that Mexican authorities explain the
situation so that caravan members make decisions with information about their
prospects of entry.

Asked explicitly whether there would be acts of repression against migrants,
Sheinbaum answered no and reiterated that the institutions’ actions will focus
on informing, accompanying and guaranteeing basic care during their journey
through the country.
